How I Think

AI created leverage.
I used it to focus on people, not paperwork.

By automating research, preparation, follow-up, CRM hygiene, and administrative work, I was able to spend more time building trust, understanding customers, solving problems, and moving opportunities forward.

01

I start by identifying the real bottleneck, not the obvious one. At Papaya, the problem was not effort. It was context switching and specification fidelity across multiple product lines, global buyers, and no SDR support.

02

Before prompting anything, I designed a pipeline. What data goes in, what judgment is required, what the output looks like, and how success is measured.

03

Each morning the system pulled from live data sources, ranked the highest-signal targets, routed outreach by channel, and generated call preparation before I opened my laptop.

04

That freed me to do what AI cannot do. Be present with clients, ask better questions, open markets, and move complex deals forward.

05

The system was not a sales tool. It was an operating layer. The Daily Briefing, post-call engine, internal communications skill, and maintenance dashboard helped turn scattered work into a repeatable operating rhythm.

Case Studies

Selected work that shows
how I operate.

These are not every deal I touched. They are the clearest examples of pattern recognition, enterprise selling, strategy, and learning.

Trigger-event selling

Moniepoint

$886K opportunity, preferred provider pending approval. I identified a senior payroll leadership hire, formed a hypothesis around scaling pain, waited for the right timing, built a champion relationship, mapped stakeholders, and coordinated executive sponsorship.

  • Strategic prospecting
  • Stakeholder mapping
  • Executive alignment
Enterprise opportunity creation

Reliance Industries

$200K+ land-and-expand opportunity, proposal under review. Reliance entered my pipeline through cold outbound. I built the HR relationship, led discovery and validation, coordinated solutions support, and delivered a tailored proposal.

  • Cold outbound into global enterprise
  • Multi-stage evaluation
  • Commercial and technical coordination
Market expansion

Africa GTM Strategy

Drawing on years of investing and operating across Africa, I built a continent-wide GTM framework covering market prioritization, partnerships, startup ecosystems, government relationships, and enterprise expansion.

  • Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa
  • Enterprise, providers, startups, governments
  • Strategy and execution roadmap
Lessons learned

Getir

Getir came through outbound and evolved into a competitive procurement process. We lost to a cheaper provider, but the lesson was valuable: strategic logos need earlier executive sponsorship and intentional pricing strategy.

  • Procurement-led evaluation
  • Land-and-expand thinking
  • Executive sponsorship lesson
Philosophy
The gap between 80% and 99% is not better prompts. It is system architecture.

I am interested in using AI to improve execution quality, decision-making, and organizational leverage. The value is not the technology itself. The value is what it enables people and organizations to accomplish.
